description: Eight scenarios for user-wrap's four verdict paths, including foreign fallback state and three incomplete WRAP & CLOSE outcomes. Every scenario is graded against all 10 assertions; conditional assertions are vacuously true when their banner is absent.

scenarios.name: Operator sits back down after a break, mid-task -> KEEP GOING, execute Next Action with no ask
scenarios.description: The most common verdict. Orient-lite must come first (assertion 1), the verdict must arrive via a delegated session-wrap --advise run (assertion 2), the KEEP GOING banner + loss report are re-presented verbatim (assertions 4, 5), and the Next Action executes immediately with no confirmation ask (assertion 6). Nothing mutates before the banner (assertion 10) and no user-wrap-authored threshold prose appears (assertion 3). Actively exercises assertions 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10; the golden anchor is golden/good_keep_going.md. Assertion 6 also grades the paired locked-bundle condition: a task-handoff-next-action-v1 bundle from the own file must be printed and held, never executed.
scenarios.context: Operator returns after ~40 minutes away to an open Alpha4Gate window and types '/user-wrap' ('sitting back down - keep going or wrap?'). This session's own sessions/<session-id>.md: Task 'build-phase | Alpha4Gate reward-shaping phase, step 4 of 9', Status IN_PROGRESS, Last written 2026-07-13T17:20:00Z (fresh per the schema doc), Session SHA f3a91d2 matches HEAD; Next Action 'uv run pytest tests/test_rewards.py -q, then continue /build-step --plan docs/plans/alpha4gate-plan.md --step 4'. Git: Alpha4Gate master @ f3a91d2, 2 dirty files (bot/rewards.py, tests/test_rewards.py), 1 ahead (last push landed 9d41c2e). A /goal is armed and unmet ('12 eval games green'). The delegated session-wrap --advise resolves the signal cleanly at 84,300 tokens (~42% assuming a 200k window), reports mid-task, and would route continue -> verdict KEEP GOING. Correct output: orientation block, the advise triage line + KEEP GOING banner + two-line loss report verbatim, then immediate execution of the Next Action with no confirmation ask. Conditional locked-bundle variant for assertion 6: replace the plain Next Action with a task-handoff-next-action-v1 bundle; correct behavior prints it verbatim, emits 'Locked bundle held (not executed by user-wrap).', and stops without execution.

scenarios.name: Return right after a step flipped DONE, heavy context -> RECYCLE WINDOW, invoke bare /session-wrap
scenarios.description: The recycle path. --advise would route clear-next, so the banner is RECYCLE WINDOW and user-wrap's action is to invoke bare /session-wrap via the Skill tool — which then acts itself (durable write, render, git verb, Pick-up-here block ending in /clear). user-wrap adds nothing between banner and loss report and runs no git verb of its own before the banner. Actively exercises assertions 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 10; the golden anchor is golden/good_recycle_window.md.
scenarios.context: toybox plan step 12 of 14 flipped DONE just before the operator stepped away for dinner; they return and type '/user-wrap - should I keep going or wrap up?'. This session's own sessions/<session-id>.md: Task 'build-phase | toybox plan, step 12 of 14', Status IN_PROGRESS (boundary write already set Next Action '/build-step --plan docs/plans/toybox-plan.md --step 13'), Last written 2026-07-13T23:05:00Z (fresh), Session SHA a7c22b1 matches HEAD. Git: toybox master @ a7c22b1, 3 dirty files (app/propose.py, app/judge.py, tests/test_propose.py), 0 ahead. No armed /goal. The delegated --advise reports 141,200 tokens (~71% assuming a 200k window) at the step boundary and would route clear-next -> verdict RECYCLE WINDOW. Correct action: invoke bare /session-wrap (it acts); its output — its own triage line, written own-session checkpoint, regenerated rollup, rendered handoff-prompt.md, per-repo git verb, Pick-up-here block whose next command is /clear — follows the re-presented report.

scenarios.name: Next-morning return, task COMPLETE, one unpushed commit + one unfiled TODO -> WRAP & CLOSE, invoke /session-wrap --end
scenarios.description: The wrap path. Triage would route end-window AND the salvage preview is non-empty (an unpushed commit + an unfiled TODO), so the banner is WRAP & CLOSE and user-wrap invokes /session-wrap --end. The loss report's concrete anchors (SHA, counts, the TODO's identity) must survive re-presentation untouched — this is the scenario where paraphrasing or burying the loss report does the most damage. Actively exercises assertions 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10; the golden anchor is golden/good_wrap_close.md. Its own-session Next Action is a locked task-handoff-next-action-v1 bundle, so the delegated render and opener must preserve it as held data for the owning dispatcher rather than execute or flatten it.
scenarios.context: Operator returns the next morning to a window left open overnight on shake_spear and types '/user-wrap - am I safe to close this window?'. This session's own sessions/<session-id>.md: Task 'repo-update | shake_spear v1 wrap', Status COMPLETE (v1 wrapped last night; the remaining work is operator M1 UAT #15 - an operator boundary, no agent-completable next action), Last written 2026-07-13T03:40:00Z (7h ago - fresh per the schema doc's staleness threshold), Session SHA d81f3a0 matches HEAD. Git: shake_spear master @ d81f3a0, 0 dirty, 1 ahead (last night's wrap commit d81f3a0 never reached origin - the push failed silently). The delegated --advise reports 58,900 tokens (~29% assuming a 200k window), would route end-window, and its salvage preview finds two at-risk items: the unpushed commit and 1 unfiled TODO from scrollback (the ss CLI --seed flag accepts out-of-range values; never parked, never filed) -> verdict WRAP & CLOSE. Correct action: re-present the banner + loss report verbatim, then invoke /session-wrap --end automatically with no confirmation ask (the full end-window wrap follows: memory pass, render, git verb, Pick-up-here block with the fresh-window opener), and close with the exact plain line 'RAN SESSION-WRAP & SAFE TO CLOSE'. The render labels the bundle data-only and the owner-bound opener reports that its owning dispatcher is required; neither uses generic execute-Next-Action wording.

scenarios.name: Next-morning return, everything durable -> SAFE TO CLOSE, one-liner then stop
scenarios.description: The stop path — the verdict where doing MORE is the defect. Every no-op condition holds (clean tree, origin in sync, no armed /goal, own session file fresh + consistent, salvage preview empty), so the banner is SAFE TO CLOSE with 'Dies with this window: nothing', and user-wrap prints exactly one all-durable closing line and stops: no /session-wrap invocation, no task-handoff invocation, no git verb, no Pick-up-here block. Actively exercises assertions 1, 2, 4, 5, 9, 10; the golden anchor is golden/good_safe_close.md.
scenarios.context: Same next-morning shake_spear shape, all clear: the operator returns and types '/user-wrap - am I safe to close this window?'. This session's own sessions/<session-id>.md: Task 'repo-update | shake_spear v1 wrap', Status COMPLETE, Last written 2026-07-13T03:40:00Z (7h ago - fresh per the schema doc), Session SHA d81f3a0 matches HEAD. Git: shake_spear master @ d81f3a0, 0 dirty, 0 ahead - origin in sync (last night's push landed). No armed /goal. The delegated --advise reports 61,300 tokens (~31% assuming a 200k window), would route end-window as a NO-OP: every durable condition holds and the salvage preview is empty -> verdict SAFE TO CLOSE, 'Dies with this window: nothing'. Correct action: re-present the banner + loss report, then ONE closing line stating everything is durable and the window can be closed - and STOP.

scenarios.name: WRAP & CLOSE stops at the parallel-session ask
scenarios.description: A foreign commit on another local branch makes session-wrap's anomaly pre-flight return ask-first pending. Its ask response remains the last output; user-wrap neither answers it nor prints SAFE TO CLOSE.
scenarios.context: Use the wrap-close morning case, but seed a foreign commit on another local branch within the last hour. The Step D segment is exactly 'ask-first pending'. Correct output invokes /session-wrap --end, ends with session-wrap's ask response, and adds no user-wrap line.

scenarios.name: WRAP & CLOSE reports a rejected push without claiming safety
scenarios.description: A deterministic local remote rejects the base-action push. The setup commit is pushed before the rejection hook is installed; a later dirty session edit is committed by session-wrap, so the rejected operation cannot be confused with the clean-but-ahead 'pushed N pending' case.
scenarios.context: Start from a disposable repo whose setup commit is already pushed to a local bare origin. Install a pre-receive hook that exits 1, then make one tracked dirty edit. session-wrap commits that edit and reports the exact non-completed segment 'commit created @ <short-sha>; push failed: remote rejected (pre-receive hook declined)'. Correct user-wrap output quotes that segment in one line, prints no SAFE TO CLOSE line, and stops without retry.

scenarios.name: KEEP GOING treats another window's rollup as orientation only
scenarios.description: This window has no own session file. The fresh current.md rollup belongs to another session, so user-wrap labels the source and does not execute its Next Action even though --advise returns KEEP GOING. Git's raw count remains 12 dirty. An independent receipt created before the current window and outside this session's write authority binds the current identity and bytes of all 12 untracked host/runtime installation paths, so they remain context rather than current-window loss.
scenarios.context: No sessions/<this-id>.md exists, so session identity and boundary state are unavailable. current.md contains another session's fresh Next Action. Git porcelain contains 12 untracked host/runtime installation entries. An independent receipt created before the current window and outside this session's write authority names all 12 paths and binds each current identity and bytes; the current window created or modified none of them. A path/category label or a ledger writable in the current window would not suffice. Correct output includes 'state: current.md rollup — not this session's own; orientation only'; keeps '12 dirty' in both raw Git segments; emits the exact unavailable-context signal and an unknown boundary with identity unavailable; names the count and independent proof basis in 'Already durable:'; re-presents KEEP GOING with 'Dies with this window: nothing'; then prints 'Next Action not run: state is the current.md rollup; orientation only.' and stops.

scenarios.name: WRAP & CLOSE preserves an unwritten checkpoint in the current window
scenarios.description: task-handoff returns a non-success line during session-wrap --end. No render or opener is presented and no safety line follows; session-wrap's in-window re-run step is last.
scenarios.context: The session file write cannot complete and task-handoff returns 'Checkpoint not written: required_tool_missing (session identity).'. Correct output contains session-wrap's pointer 'Full handoff: not rendered this turn (checkpoint not written)' and ends with its fenced /session-wrap --end re-run step. user-wrap appends nothing.
